verdict.rationale: Yapily documents a dedicated re-authorise account consent endpoint for when a previously AUTHORIZED consent can no longer be used to retrieve data. That is a first-party repair flow that re-prompts the account holder instead of starting from scratch. The evidence only implies consent statuses through the AUTHORIZED state; it does not document specific expired or revoked statuses, or how broken links are surfaced to ops. Missing for 10: documented expired/revoked consent status values, proactive surfacing of broken connections (e.g., consent-expiry webhook events), and hands-on corroboration of the re-auth flow preserving existing linkage.

support.subject: As an ops lead, broken connections are repairable — expired or revoked links surface as documented statuses, and users can re-authenticate in an update flow without starting over

citations.quote: Used to prompt the account holder for continued access to their financial data. This endpoint should be used when a `Consent` that was previously `AUTHORIZED` can no longer be used to retrieve data.
